author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
Hardware engineers are NOT so safe from AI after all.

GPT 5.6 Sol was able to one shot a 74181 in 45 minutes for $35. It comes with an implementation plan, test plan, formal plan, UVM TB, formal assertions and 100% coverage.

Opus 5 finally finished the task the next morning spending almost $700.

Sonnet 5 and Luna are hopeless, we can write them off in hardware design work.

Next I am going to try the run on some open source models.

comments.text: A human need to confirm if AI did the job or not. With 20% hallucination possibility we cannot leave the validation and quality aspects to other AI models/agents. So, number of hardware engineers working on a spec may reduce, but now these hardware engineers can spend more time creating new specs.

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

replies.text: Ravikumar M. how many spec does the world really need?

author.name: Ravikumar M.
author.headline: Solution Architect, Tech Mahindra

replies.text: Horace Chan I think there are many areas. High performance cheap Hardware can reduce costs drastically while gaining on time. We saw that with USB, Microprocessors etc.. As far as I know, not everything is moved into hardware, we have some processing power, communication tech, memory moved into hardware with some peripherals. The complexity to test & debug makes the process slow to move for other systems to migrate. I think with AI most of these things can gain speed, so innovators can free their mind from testing, debugging and think about improving processes in other areas. For example AI inference, edge computing, digital twins with sensors in real systems etc are possible.

author.name: Mika Nyström
author.headline: Chip architect

replies.text: Ravikumar M. Well 74181, that's the 4-bit ALU, right? (Not sure why I would remember that but I think that's what it was.) That's easily small enough that even naive formal verification can validate the design. So you don't really need humans for this task. This gets a lot more interesting if the design can loop and has a lot of state. In those cases, you can use AI to create a correctness proof that you check against the spec and RTL. So the only thing you should have to check by human is the spec. What's important there is that if it's a large system, you really should only have to check the spec at the perimeter of the system, not at every internal module boundary. Well, holy grail and all that. But I'm cautiously optimistic 😁

author.name: Ravikumar M.
author.headline: Solution Architect, Tech Mahindra

replies.text: Mika Nyström Yes, specs and gaurdrails - that is what makes the whole process controlled & manageable.
